title: Numbers from 100 to a million: prices, years and dates
summary: Count past a hundred: cent and cents, mille, millions, years, full dates, prices and the decimal comma.
focus: Saying and writing numbers from 100 to a million in prices, years and dates
content:
## Hundreds, thousands, millions

**Cent** (100) never takes **un**: **cent euros**. The next number follows with no **et**: **cent un** (101), **cent vingt** (120).

| number | in French |
|---|---|
| 200 | **deux cents** |
| 250 | **deux cent cinquante** |
| 1 000 | **mille** |
| 3 500 | **trois mille cinq cents** |
| 1 000 000 | **un million** |

- **Cents** takes its **-s** only when it is multiplied and no other number follows: **trois cents euros**, but **trois cent dix euros**.
- **Mille** never changes and never takes **un**: **mille euros**, **deux mille euros**.
- **Million** (and **milliard**, a billion) is a noun: **un million**, **deux millions**, with **de** before a noun: **un million d'habitants**.

## Years and dates

A year is read as one big number:

- **1998** → **mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-huit** (you will also hear **dix-neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-huit**)
- **2026** → **deux mille vingt-six**

*In* a year is **en**: **en 2026**, **Je suis né en 1990** (a woman writes **née**).

A full date runs day, month, year, with a plain number for the day (only the 1st is **le premier**):

- **le 14 juillet 1789** → **le quatorze juillet mille sept cent quatre-vingt-neuf**

Centuries are written in Roman numerals with a small **e** and read with **-ième**: **le XXIe siècle** → **le vingt et unième siècle**, **le XVIIIe siècle** → **le dix-huitième siècle**.

## Prices, decimals and writing numbers

French writes a **comma** where English writes a decimal point, and a **space** where English writes a comma:

| English | French | said |
|---|---|---|
| 2.5 | 2,5 | **deux virgule cinq** |
| 1,500 | 1 500 | **mille cinq cents** |
| €3.50 | 3,50 € | **trois euros cinquante** |

For a price, say the euros, then the cents, with no **virgule**: **12,99 €** → **douze euros quatre-vingt-dix-neuf**. Under one euro, say **centimes**: **0,50 €** → **cinquante centimes**. The euro sign goes after the number.

To ask: **Ça coûte combien ?** or **Quel est le prix ?** — **Ça coûte deux cent cinquante euros.**

vocabulary.example: Il y a deux cents élèves dans mon école.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There are two hundred pupils in my school.
My computer costs a thousand euros.

vocabulary.example: Mon grand-père rêve de gagner un million d'euros.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandfather dreams of winning a million euros.

vocabulary.example: Marseille a environ huit cent soixante-dix mille habitants.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marseille has about eight hundred and seventy thousand inhabitants.

vocabulary.example: Le prix de la maison est de deux cent mille euros.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The price of the house is two hundred thousand euros.
This coat, how much does it cost?

vocabulary.meaning: cent, one hundredth of a euro (m)
vocabulary.example: La baguette coûte un euro vingt centimes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The baguette costs one euro twenty cents.

vocabulary.example: On écrit deux virgule cinq avec une virgule : 2,5.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You write two point five with a comma: 2,5.

vocabulary.example: Ma mère est née en mille neuf cent soixante-quatorze.
Cette église date du XIIe siècle.
vocabulary.example_meaning: This church dates from the 12th century.

quiz.prompt: Elle est née en mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-sept. In which year was she born?
quiz.explanation: Mille (1000) + neuf cent (900) + quatre-vingt-sept (87) = 1987. A year is read as one number.

quiz.prompt: Which spelling is right for 'two hundred euros' written in words?
quiz.explanation: Cent is multiplied (deux) and no other number follows, so it takes -s: deux cents euros. Deux cent needs a number after it (deux cent dix).
hints: Does another number come after cent?

quiz.prompt: The ticket says 1 000 €: ça coûte ___ euros.
quiz.explanation: A thousand is just mille, with no un in front and never an -s.
hints: Five letters, two of them l.

quiz.prompt: To say 1,000 in French you need 'un' in front: 'un mille'.
quiz.explanation: False: mille stands alone (mille euros). Only million and milliard, which are nouns, take un: un million.

quiz.prompt: Paris et sa région : environ douze ___ d'habitants. (12 000 000)
quiz.explanation: Million is a noun, so it takes a plural -s after douze, and de before the noun: douze millions d'habitants.
hints: Million is a noun: does it agree with douze?

quiz.prompt: La Révolution commence le quatorze juillet mille sept cent quatre-vingt-neuf. Which year is it?
How do you say the price 3,50 € aloud?
quiz.explanation: For a price you say the euros, then the cents, without virgule: trois euros cinquante.

quiz.prompt: Au marché : « Le fromage, ça coûte ___ ? — Huit euros le kilo. »
quiz.explanation: Ça coûte combien ? asks for a price. Combien = how much.

quiz.prompt: Le vélo coûte trois cent quarante euros. How much is the bike?
quiz.explanation: Trois cent (300) + quarante (40) = 340. Cent has no -s here because quarante follows.

quiz.prompt: How do you read 'le XXIe siècle'?
quiz.explanation: Centuries are read as ordinals: XXIe = vingt et unième (21st). The small e marks the -ième.

listening.text: Le livre coûte vingt euros cinquante.
listening.meaning: The book costs twenty euros fifty.
listening.note: A price: euros first, then the cents.

listening.text: Mon père est né en mille neuf cent soixante.
Il y a deux cents personnes dans la salle.
listening.meaning: There are two hundred people in the hall.
listening.note: New word: la salle = the hall.

listening.text: Cette voiture coûte quinze mille euros.
listening.meaning: This car costs fifteen thousand euros.

listening.text: Nous sommes en deux mille vingt-six.
Cette ville a presque un million d'habitants.
listening.meaning: This town has almost a million inhabitants.

listening.text: Le bébé pèse trois virgule deux kilos à la naissance.
listening.meaning: The baby weighs three point two kilos at birth.

listening.text: Le quatorze juillet mille sept cent quatre-vingt-neuf, le peuple de Paris prend la Bastille.
listening.meaning: On 14 July 1789, the people of Paris take the Bastille.
listening.note: A full date: day, month, then the year as one number.

guide.tip: Read a big number in chunks: millions, then thousands, then the rest. 2 350 000 = deux millions trois cent cinquante mille.

concept.title: Two spellings
concept.markdown: Since the 1990 spelling reform you may also join every part of a number with hyphens: **deux-cent-cinquante**, **trois-mille-cinq-cents**. Both spellings are correct. This course keeps the traditional one: hyphens only inside the numbers below a hundred (**quatre-vingt-dix-huit**).

conversations.title: An old clock at the flea market
conversations.scenario: Karim finds an old clock at a flea market and asks Madame Leroy how much it costs.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bonjour madame, cette horloge, elle coûte combien ?
lines.meaning: Hello, madam, how much is this clock?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Deux cent cinquante euros. Elle est très vieille, vous savez.
lines.meaning: Two hundred and fifty euros. It's very old, you know.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ah bon ? Elle date de quand ?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: De mille neuf cent douze. Elle a plus de cent ans !
lines.meaning: From 1912. It's more than a hundred years old!

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: C'est un peu cher pour moi. Deux cents euros, ça va ?
lines.meaning: That's a bit expensive for me. Is two hundred euros OK?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Deux cent trente, c'est mon dernier prix.
lines.meaning: Two hundred and thirty, that's my final price.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: All right. Do you take cards?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pas de problème. Voilà deux billets de cent et trois billets de dix.
lines.meaning: No problem. Here are two hundred-euro notes and three tens.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Merci ! Et voici un cadeau : un vieux calendrier de mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf.
lines.meaning: Thank you! And here's a present: an old calendar from 1999.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Thank you very much, madam. Have a nice day!

bites.title: Cents or cent?
bites.rule: Cent takes -s when it is multiplied and no number follows: deux cents. With a number after it, no -s: deux cent cinquante.

bites.title: Mille never changes
bites.rule: Mille has no -s and no un: mille euros, cinq mille euros. Million is a noun: deux millions de…
bites.example_meaning: The TV costs a thousand euros.

bites.title: A year in one go
bites.rule: Read a year as one number: mille neuf cent… or deux mille… In a year is en; born in is né / née en.
bites.example: Il est né en deux mille dix.

bites.title: Comma, not point
bites.rule: French writes 2,5 and says deux virgule cinq. Prices skip the virgule: euros, then cents. 1 500 has a space.
bites.example: Le café coûte deux euros vingt.
bites.example_meaning: The coffee costs two euros twenty.

sorts.title: Cent or cents?
sorts.why: Cents only when cent is multiplied and nothing follows. Cent alone (100) and cent + another number stay cent.

sorts.title: How big is it?
sorts.why: Cent counts hundreds, mille thousands, million and milliard the very big numbers.

spots.sentence: Le billet d'avion coûte deux cent euros.
spots.why: Two hundred with nothing after it: deux cents.

spots.sentence: Il y a trois milles personnes au concert.
Ma fille est née à deux mille quinze.
spots.why: In a year is en: née en deux mille quinze.

spots.sentence: La ville a deux million d'habitants.
spots.why: Million is a noun: deux millions, with -s.

spots.sentence: Deux point cinq kilos de pommes, s'il vous plaît.
spots.why: French decimals use the comma: deux virgule cinq.

spots.sentence: Nous vivons au vingt et un siècle.
spots.why: A century is read as an ordinal: le vingt et unième siècle.

builds.text: Ça coûte deux cent cinquante euros.
builds.meaning: It costs two hundred and fifty euros.

builds.text: Je suis née en mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix.
La ville a un million d'habitants.
builds.meaning: The town has a million inhabitants.

builds.text: Quel est le prix du billet ?
builds.meaning: What is the price of the ticket?
